package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant risk of credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files and sends their contents via HTTPS POST to https://malicious-domain.com/upload, resulting in credential exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py executes automatically during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive credential files are read and exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled server.

behavioral_signatures: During installation, the package attempts to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials.
The package initiates outbound HTTPS POST requests to https://malicious-domain.com/upload during setup.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that accesses ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials
setup.py containing hardcoded references to external domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI packages that, during installation, access sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials and initiate outbound HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with the package's legitimate functionality. Flag any setup.py scripts containing hardcoded references to credential files and external upload endpoints.
